reason: This passage from Genesis 27 depicts Yahweh as favorable and providential toward Jacob (Israel). Jacob explicitly attributes his success to Yahweh's assistance ('because Yahweh your God brought it about before me'). The text presents Isaac's blessing as divinely enabled, conferring dominion, prosperity, and the devotion of nations and peoples. Jacob receives abundant blessings—grain, wine, the homage of brothers and nations, and protection from curses. Throughout the narrative, Yahweh's will appears to be actively advancing Jacob's position as the chosen heir, not opposing him or the Hebrew people. There is no indication of divine antagonism toward Jacob or hostility from Yahweh in this account.
